newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-RAIN POSTPONES HONDA CLASSIC SECOND ROUND.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-RAIN POSTPONES HONDA CLASSIC SECOND ROUND.

text.p: Morning rainstorms prevented play on Friday at the Honda Classic, forcing the second round to be postponed until Saturday.
Although the greens and bunkers drained well, the rain flooded the fairways at the TPC at Heron Bay, leaving the course unplayable.
The PGA Tour has not yet determined whether the tournament will be played to a full 72 holes or cut to 54 holes.
After the first round, the leaders were 1993 U.S. Open champion Lee Janzen and this year's Hawaiian Open winner, Paul Stankowski, both at five under par.
Britain's Colin Montgomerie, Payne Stewart, Greg Kraft, Billy Ray Brown and Stuart Appleby of Australia were a stroke behind after opening rounds of four-under 68.
